description: Anger controlling you is sin. But anger itself is not. There is a difference — and this verse tells you exactly what to do with it.
excerpt: Sleep on it. And be quiet in the meantime. That is such practical wisdom. Especially the silent part.
verse: "Don't sin by letting anger control you. Think about it overnight and remain silent."
body_html:
First off: anger controlling you is sin.

That is what this verse actually says. It doesn't say anger is sin. It doesn't say you can't feel it. It says don't let it control you. There is a difference between feeling anger and letting anger have you.

And then it says something that I don't remember reading before.

Think about it overnight and remain silent.

Sleep on it. And be quiet in the meantime.

That is such practical wisdom. Especially the silent part. Because when I'm angry, the last thing I want to do is be quiet. My instinct is to talk, defend myself, tell my side, and explain exactly why I'm right. I want to pick up my phone and type a reply immediately.

But the verse says wait. Sleep first. Do not react in the middle of it.

Now I know there is another verse people quote all the time from Ephesians. Do not let the sun go down on your anger. That one is important too. It is warning us not to let anger take root and turn into bitterness. Not to carry it for days and weeks and years. Not to nurse it and feed it and let it become part of who we are.

Both are true.

I actually think they work together.

Sometimes a good night of sleep does something to anger that arguing in the moment never could. It gives the anger a chance to settle. Your brain gets to actually process what happened instead of just reacting to it. Most of the time, what felt so intense at ten p.m. doesn't feel nearly as sharp at seven a.m.

Silence and sleep have a way of separating the truth from the emotion.

And on the other side, the Ephesians principle keeps the sleeping honest. You aren't sleeping on it so you can bury it and pretend it didn't happen. You are sleeping on it so you can wake up and handle it well. There is still a job to do. You still have to address the thing. You just address it with a calmer head.

That is the balance.

Feel your anger. Do not deny it or stuff it. But don't let it run the show or stay past its welcome. Sleep on it. Stay quiet. Come back and deal with it with a clearer head. Then let it go.

If we really lived by this verse, so many of our relationships would look different.

Most of the damage we do when we are angry could have been avoided if we had just been quiet long enough for the fire to cool.

The silent part is the hard part.

That is really what I struggle with. It is one thing to say I'm going to sleep on it. It is another thing to actually not say a word until you have. Not send the text, fire off the email or vent to a friend just to keep it going. Not stew out loud and replay over and over. Silent means silent.

I want to be that kind of person.

The kind who feels it honestly, sits with it, sleeps on it, and handles it with a clear heart instead of a hot one.

That isn't weakness. It is wisdom.
question: What is something you have been angry about that could probably use a night of sleep and some silence before you respond?
